title: Quant junction: arithmetic fusion and prefill pacing to reduce quant-cast overhead
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Our current runtime performs explicit cast/convert operations frequently between INT8/FP8 and FP16 during the prefill and decode code paths. For streaming decode and short-prefill workloads this shows up as repeated quantize/dequantize work and kernel-selection churn that inflates per-token latency and increases GPU memory traffic.

Goal: Reduce end-to-end cast overhead by introducing a "quant junction" strategy: (1) fused arithmetic kernels that operate directly on quantized buffers for the hot QKV + matmul + attention epilogue patterns, (2) a prefill pacing policy that aligns microbatches and KV layout to minimize kernel switching, and (3) propagation of scale metadata through the scheduling layer so we avoid redundant scale/reshard ops.

Non-goals: This ticket does not attempt a model-rewrite for quant-aware training or change model weights. It targets runtime behavior and scheduling only. It will not implement full INT4 support yet.

Design summary:
- Introduce fused CUDA kernels (prototype) that combine: quantized GEMM (INT8/FP8 input) -> accumulation -> scaled reorder -> optional bias/add -> attention softmax-ready layout. These kernels accept a lightweight scale descriptor so they can compute with integer accumulators and produce packed quant outputs without intermediate host-side casts.
- Extend kernel selection to choose fused path when: contiguous quant buffers are present, microbatch size <= N (configurable), and KV cache layout allows in-place packing. Fall back to generic FP path otherwise.
- Implement prefill pacing: during multi-request prefill we adjust the scheduler to aggregate microbatches into a single fused prefill window when possible. The scheduler will pause non-fused tasks briefly (configurable latency budget) to complete a fused-prefill batch and write quant-packed KV to the cache, reducing repeated conversions on subsequent decodes.
- Propagate scale/zero-point metadata with buffer descriptors across the runtime so kernels can decide if a no-op conversion is needed. This avoids recomputing scale factors per token.

Telemetry and metrics to add:
- quant_cast_rate: fraction of tokens that undergo explicit cast ops in the pipeline
- kernel_switch_count: per-request count of kernel format switches (quant->fp16->quant)
- fused_prefill_hit: boolean per-request whether the fused prefill path was used
- avg_cast_time_ms: avg time spent in cast kernels per request
- token_throughput_fused_vs_baseline: curated perf benchmark metric

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spike: implement a prototype fused QKV+epilogue CUDA kernel in a sandboxed branch. Verify correctness vs FP baseline on a 7B model. (owner: Alejandro)
2) Runtime: extend buffer descriptor to carry scale metadata and a new kernel capability flag (quant-fused-ready). Update kernel selector to prefer fused kernels when capability matches. (owner: Maya)
3) Scheduler: implement prefill pacing policy that groups prefill microbatches for short sequences. Provide opt-in feature-flag. (owner: Leah Patel)
4) Telemetry: add metrics and dashboards. Run perf harness across model sizes (7B/13B/34B) and microbatch patterns. (owner: Metric team)
5) Integration & tests: unit tests for metadata propagation, integration perf tests for streaming decode, accuracy regression tests on a small eval set. (owner: QA/Eng)

Benchmarks to run: baseline vs fused path on representative workloads: chat (prefill=64 tokens, decode=1 token streaming), summarization (prefill=512), and short-burst queries (prefill=8). Track p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput. Target is >= 12% token throughput improvement on 7B streaming workloads and >= 8% p99 reduction for small-prefill 13B.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fused kernels produce bit-compatible logits within acceptable tolerance (no >0.3% top-1 divergence for eval prompts)
- End-to-end token throughput improved by >=12% for target workloads in perf harness
- p99 latency for 1-token streaming decode reduced by >=8% on at least one model size
- Telemetry is available and shows quant_cast_rate drop of >=30% on canary traffic
- Feature is gated behind runtime flag and canary rollout plan exists

Risks and mitigation:
- Accuracy regressions from quantized epilogue: mitigate by running prioritized eval harness and keeping fallback to FP path; add a per-customer safety flag to disable fused path if quality drops.
- Kernel complexity causing regressions on certain GPUs: start with a narrow list of tested GPUs (A100/H100) and enable others after validation.
- Scheduler-induced latency spikes when grouping microbatches: enforce strict latency budget and expose config to tune grouping thresholds.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 0: internal perf experiments and correctness validation (sandbox branch)
- Stage 1: internal canary with non-critical internal teams using a runtime flag (1% traffic) and dashboards monitoring token_throughput and quant_cast_rate
- Stage 2: expand to PLG customers with opt-in flags and telemetry checks
- Stage 3: full on-by-default rollout if metrics are stable for 2 weeks

Next steps / open questions:
- Decide the microbatch grouping policy threshold (initial proposal: group up to 4 microbatches or up to 32 extra ms of queuing).
- Confirm whether HLO changes are required for models that embed scale factors in attention kernels.
- Determine whether to add an explicit metadata field for per-head scale vs per-tensor scale (prefer per-tensor initially).

Estimated effort breakdown: prototype kernel (2w), selector & descriptor changes (1w), scheduler changes + tests (1w), perf runs & dashboards (1w).
